What is the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis code for this patient?

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient Name: [REDACTED]

Age: 70 years

Sex: Male

Medical History:

The patient was diagnosed with advanced renal cell carcinoma and was receiving Ipilimumab/Nivolumab therapy. He presented with new-onset fatigue and dizziness after two cycles of therapy.

Hospital Course:

During the hospital course, the patient underwent a physical examination, which revealed normal visual fields. Laboratory assessment showed mild hyponatremia, with low TSH and free T4. Morning ACTH and cortisol were also low. MRI brain showed pituitary enhancement.
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Treatment:

Ipilimumab/Nivolumab therapy was temporarily stopped, and the patient was started on hydrocortisone 10mg/5mg in the morning and afternoon, respectively, as well as a weight-based dose of levothyroxine. The patient demonstrated clinical improvement and was restarted on PD-1 monotherapy.

Follow-up:

The patient was given "sick day" instructions for stress dosing of hydrocortisone and a medical alert bracelet. Key concepts of management involve high index of clinical suspicion, appropriate localization of endocrine dysfunction, hormone replacement, and close monitoring. Immune-related endocrine events are unique as the manifestations are often irreversible, and patients often require lifelong hormone replacement.

Hospital Disposition:

The patient was discharged from the hospital after clinical improvement. It is recommended that ICI is held for any-grade hypophysitis. Once patients demonstrate stability on hormonal replacement, ICI can be restarted. Higher-grade hypophysitis can be managed with an initial pulsed dose of corticosteroids. The patient was instructed to continue receiving follow-up medical care.

text:
# Principal diagnosis: **E23.1 – Drug-induced hypopituitarism**

## Clinical picture

The patient has **immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced hypophysitis** caused by ipilimumab/nivolumab. The evidence is:

- **Central (secondary) adrenal insufficiency**: low morning ACTH and low cortisol.
- **Central hypothyroidism**: low TSH and low free T4.
- **Hyponatraemia**, consistent with cortisol deficiency.
- **Pituitary enhancement on MRI**.
- **Temporal link** to the drug, with onset after two cycles of ipilimumab/nivolumab.
- **Treatment directed at the hypopituitarism**: hormone replacement with hydrocortisone and levothyroxine.

## Why E23.1 is the principal diagnosis

- The hypophysitis has caused deficiency of more than one pituitary axis (ACTH and TSH). That makes this a hypopituitary state.
- A drug caused it, and E23.1 captures both the pituitary failure and the drug cause.
- E23.1 is more specific than E23.6 (Other disorders of pituitary gland, the index default for "hypophysitis"). E23.6 would fit an inflamed pituitary without stated drug-induced hormone failure.
- This was an adverse effect of a correctly prescribed and administered drug, not a poisoning. So the condition is the principal diagnosis, with an external cause code added. A T-code (poisoning) is not used.

## Suggested additional codes

| Code | Description |
|---|---|
| **Y43.x** | Adverse effect of antineoplastic/immunomodulating drugs in therapeutic use. Assign the specific code per your edition's Table of Drugs for ipilimumab/nivolumab (monoclonal antibody immunotherapy). |
| **Y92.x** | Place of occurrence, if required by your edition and local standards. |
| **E87.1** | Hypo-osmolality and hyponatraemia, if it meets additional diagnosis criteria. Many coders would treat it as integral to the cortisol deficiency, so check ACS 0002. |
| **C64** | Malignant neoplasm of kidney (renal cell carcinoma). Add secondary codes (C77–C79) if metastatic sites are documented. |
| **Z92.6** | Personal history of chemotherapy for neoplastic disease, or the appropriate immunotherapy status code, per local practice. |

**Note:** Codes should be confirmed against the edition of ICD-10-AM/ACS in use at your facility. The withheld diagnosis section should also be checked to confirm the clinician documented "hypophysitis/hypopituitarism secondary to ipilimumab/nivolumab."
